considered.name: Deficit-Weighted Working-Capital Depletion
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when their working-capital buffer has fallen substantially from its recent peak and accumulated earned capital is weak.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the low-coverage post-payout cash-flow construction with a balance-sheet liquidity-depletion mechanism using broadly reported fields. Retained earnings only weight the signed depletion signal, so they contribute no standalone score when working capital remains near its normal level.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current-Claim Payout Capacity Gap
considered.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(MUL(RATIO(SUB(dvc, SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at)))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RANK(RATIO(lct, at))), 1))
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when distributions are large relative to after-tax operating capacity and the current-claim burden is high.
considered.reasoning: The signed numerator measures payout minus after-tax operating capacity, eliminating the opposing positive dividend-yield leg and the exact negation of residual cash coverage. Current liabilities only amplify that capacity gap, while EBITDA and tax expense provide substantially broader coverage than operating cash flow.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Creditor-Funded Productivity Erosion
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when asset productivity deteriorates relative to valuation while creditor claims simultaneously expand.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the previously weak cash-collapse and current-claim-concentration components. A high score instead requires both declining sales generated per asset and liability growth, identifying creditor-funded operating erosion without relying on the disputed return sign of asset contraction itself.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash-Backed After-Tax Margin Recovery
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), sale), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(che, 1), lt), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms outperform when after-tax operating margins improve strongly relative to price-to-sales and cash accumulates relative to liabilities.
considered.reasoning: Cash-backed asset-productivity recovery produced strong evidence on both Fama-MacBeth and FF5-alpha metrics; this tests the complementary margin channel of operating improvement. Cash accumulation confirms that the valuation-scaled margin recovery is strengthening the creditor cushion rather than remaining an accounting-only gain.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Deteriorating Payout Capacity Trap
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dvc, MAX(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), SUB(at, at))), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), at), 1)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when dividends exceed positive after-tax operating capacity while that operating capacity is deteriorating.
considered.reasoning: The payout shortfall leg is zero for nonpayers with operating losses and becomes large only when actual distributions exceed positive operating support, avoiding an opposing standalone dividend-yield exposure. Requiring deterioration in after-tax operating return targets unsustainable payouts whose support is worsening rather than merely low.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding-Gap Productivity Trap
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(MAX(SUB(lct, act), SUB(at, at)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when valuation-scaled asset productivity deteriorates while current liabilities exceed current assets by a large amount relative to equity value.
considered.reasoning: Creditor-funded productivity erosion had a correctly signed cross-sectional slope but positive alpha, suggesting that liability growth alone may be compensated financing rather than acute distress. Requiring an actual uncovered current-claim gap instead isolates productivity deterioration occurring alongside a present liquidity shortfall.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Current-Claim Revenue Squeeze
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when sales contract sharply relative to equity value while current liabilities simultaneously increase.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the low-coverage post-payout recombination with a broadly observable operating squeeze. Rising current claims can be benign during expansion, but their conjunction with shrinking sales indicates increasing near-term obligations despite a contracting revenue base.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liquidity-Floor Productivity Recovery
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at)), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(TS_MIN(RATIO(wcap, at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms outperform when valuation-scaled asset productivity improves and even their weakest recent working-capital position remains strong.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the failed depletion-and-deficit construction rather than substituting one liquid asset for another. The productivity channel captures operating recovery, while the historical working-capital floor requires durable liquidity resilience instead of a potentially noisy distance from a recent balance-sheet peak.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Dual-DuPont Valuation Trap
considered.expression: MIN(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ebitda, MAX(txt, SUB(at, at))), sale), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale))), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(RATIO(sale, at), 1), RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), at))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms underperform when both after-tax operating margin and asset turnover deteriorate substantially relative to their valuation.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the familiar liability-reduction and external-financing channels with simultaneous erosion in the two operating components of return on assets. The standardized minimum is high only when both pricing power or cost efficiency and asset productivity weaken, identifying a broad-based operating value trap rather than a single-anomaly exposure.

critic_notes.rationale: This is a coarse restatement of the well-documented value-plus-low-leverage screen (Penman-Richardson-Tuna's negative net-debt-to-price component, Piotroski's leverage criterion), and it is largely redundant with the sharper "Near-Term Refinancing Trap" proposal in the same batch.

The hard indicator gate assigns an identical score of exactly zero to every negative-retained-earnings firm, so the short leg becomes a lump of deficit firms rather than low-cash-flow-yield firms — the resulting spread will largely reproduce the known retained-earnings/RE-to-assets effect rather than test the stated conditional cash-yield hypothesis.
This is verbatim EBITDA/enterprise value, the published enterprise-multiple anomaly (Loughran and Wellman 2011), with no cross-theme interaction at all.

Sales-to-price and net-working-capital-to-assets are each individually familiar, but their interaction as a liquidity-conditioned value screen is a defensible and internally consistent test, though the author should verify RANK's output range since a product of two centered ranks would score expensive/illiquid firms as highly as cheap/liquid ones.

This is the classic Piotroski/profitability-screened-value result in reverse, and the expected negative sign is not cleanly implied by the expression because the book-cheapness leg pushes returns positive while the loss leg pushes them negative, leaving the composite slope's sign economically ambiguous rather than predicted.

Conditioning value on short-term debt net of cash — a genuine near-term refinancing measure rather than generic leverage — is a reasonable and sign-coherent refinement, but it overlaps heavily with the batch's Solvency-Weighted proposal and with known net-debt-to-price evidence, so only one of the two should be carried forward.

Since RANK(B/M) is a bounded [0,1] positive multiplier, the signal's variation is dominated by ΔRE/at, which is essentially net income minus dividends scaled by assets — a direct rediscovery of the profitability/ROA anomaly dressed as a value interaction.

The construction is internally coherent and dimensionally consistent (dollar cash flow net of positive liability growth, scaled by market cap), and though it fuses two known effects (cash-flow yield and debt issuance), the asymmetric max(Δlt,0) deduction is a genuinely new functional form rather than a cosmetic variant of the archived cash-yield signal.

Smoothed tax expense over market cap is a well-known earnings-yield proxy (taxable-income anomaly), and the max(lt−at,0) denominator adjustment is non-zero for only a tiny sliver of firms, so the signal is effectively a rediscovery of E/P with a near-inert modifier.

The dominant signed component is −Δwcap/at, a standard working-capital accrual proxy whose documented direction implies *higher* future returns for contracting working capital, so the stated negative expected sign contradicts the expression's natural direction.

Internally consistent (high score = sales-cheap plus negative cash-flow coverage, expected to underperform) and motivated by a real diagnosis of the archived signal's FMB/alpha disagreement, though it remains a same-family reweighting of the sales-to-price leg and risks simply reproducing a cash-flow-to-current-liabilities distress screen.

The sign logic is coherent (assets-to-price rank scales a signed ROA trend, so improving cheap firms score negative), and the profitability-trend leg is distinct from the static distress legs already tested, but the 5-year TREND requirement will materially cut coverage and the assets-to-market leg conflates value with leverage.

Swapping DELTA(lt) for DELTA(lt−che) in the already-archived "Liability-Financed Cash Adjustment" is a cosmetic one-term substitution rather than a new mechanism, and the resulting construct (cash flow minus net-debt issuance, scaled by market cap) is close to standard net-payout/net-debt-issuance value measures.

This is the archived "Liquid Sales Bargain" with industry demeaning and MIN in place of MUL — a mechanically minor variant of a known sales-to-price × working-capital screen — and the stated justification about "centered ranks" is inconsistent with the [0,1] rank convention used elsewhere in the archive.

Conditioning an industry-relative EBITDA yield on the signed change in short-term-debt share is an economically distinct refinancing-fragility mechanism (not the archived liability-growth level), and the unsigned-rank × signed-change construction correctly puts cheap-and-fragile firms in the short leg, though Δ(dlc/lt) will be noisy for low-lt firms.

The construction is coherent, but Δ(act/lct) is essentially a scaled working-capital accrual, whose published sign is negative (Sloan), so the positive expected sign conflicts with a well-documented anomaly and the proposal does not address that tension.

The ABS(pi) denominator breaks the stated interpretation — a loss-making firm with positive tax expense scores high rather than low — and the change in effective tax rate is itself a published anomaly (tax expense surprise, Thomas–Zhang), so the signal is both internally inconsistent and partly a rediscovery.

This is a single-theme leverage ratio, not a cross-theme interaction, and decomposes into well-known net-debt-to-market and cash-to-price effects, making it too close to published leverage/cash-holdings anomalies to be worth a test slot.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archive components — the identical WINSOR(DELTA(act-che)/at) accrual term from "Noncash Asset Build Value Trap" (which was already weak at fmb -1.76, t-alpha -1.09) bolted onto the identical IND_RANK EBITDA-yield leg from "Maturity-Extension Operating Value" — so it is a cosmetic value-proxy swap rather than a new mechanism, and the accrual leg itself is close to the published working-capital accrual anomaly.

Changing the scaler of short-term debt from total liabilities to current liabilities is a pure denominator tweak on "Maturity-Extension Operating Value," whose evidence was insignificant on both metrics (fmb 1.13, t-alpha 1.24), so this is a cosmetic variant unlikely to change the diagnosis rather than a substantively different test.

The stated diagnosis is that all-positive value×liquidity composites deliver strong FMB slopes purely from an unconditional value tilt with negative FF5 alpha, yet the proposal reproduces exactly that structure (IND_RANK ≥ 0 multiplied by TS_RANK ≥ 0, as in "Liquid Sales Bargain"), so the conditioning term cannot change sign and the signal will again be dominated by the sales-yield leg.

The second-difference leverage term is economically distinct from the one-period DELTA(lt) and peak-distance leverage variants already in the archive, and the signed distress leg correctly makes the composite a two-sided conditional consistent with the negative expected sign, though ACCEL on annual data will be noisy.

This is close to the archive's "Continuously Health-Weighted Cash Yield" (which failed) with the yield numerator swapped from oancf to dvc and the re/at term flipped, and conditioning on dividend payers with accumulated deficits selects a thin, unstable subgroup that will drive the long leg with poor coverage.

Fundamental-earnings volatility is a genuinely different distress channel from the levels, trends, leverage and liquidity terms already tested, and the industry z-scored, sign-centered construction properly makes book cheapness an amplifier rather than a standalone value tilt; the main weakness is that a 3-period VOL estimate is a very noisy volatility proxy and earnings volatility on its own is a documented anomaly.

This is the archived "Post-Deleveraging Sales Value" mechanism with only normalization swaps (IND_RANK→TS_RANK, RANK→IND_ZSCORE), so it is a largely cosmetic rescaling of a construct that already failed on alpha, and because TS_RANK is strictly positive the signal's sign is driven almost entirely by the deleveraging z-score leg rather than by any genuine interaction.

The lct/lt maturity-concentration level is a genuinely new conditioning variable in this archive (prior attempts used changes in dlc/lt or netted short-term debt), the expected negative sign is consistent with the expression, though the value leg again only scales magnitude so the test is close to a standalone debt-maturity-structure signal.

The conditioning term Δ(act−che) minus the increase in current liabilities, scaled by assets, is essentially the classic working-capital accrual measure, so despite the one-sided MAX twist this is close to a rediscovery of the Sloan accrual anomaly interacted with book-to-market.

This differs from the archived "Earnings-Instability Value Trap" only by lengthening the volatility window from 3 to 5 and switching the value leg's normalization, which is a parameter tweak rather than a substantively different mechanism addressing why the alpha was wrongly signed.

A trend in a coverage-of-current-liabilities ratio interacted with cheapness has already been tested twice in this archive (Cash-Runway Trend Value, Downside Cash-Coverage Value) with weak results, and substituting EBITDA for cash in the numerator is a cosmetic variant of the same failed family.

This wraps the archived "Uncovered Maturity Residual Yield" expression verbatim in a TS_RANK, which is a pure renormalization rather than a new mechanism, and the claim that it isolates "distress resolution" mispricing is not supported by anything the expression actually computes.

Internally consistent and a genuine re-scaling (assets → market value) that drops the value multiplier rather than a pure cosmetic tweak, but DELTA(re)/mktcap is close to a retained-earnings/E-P yield, so any strong result risks being a rediscovery of the earnings-yield anomaly rather than the conjunctive "repair" mechanism.

Sign logic is coherent, but the construction is the same denominator swap applied to a second archived signal whose evidence was insignificant on both metrics, and its two legs (price-scaled pretax earnings decline and liability growth) are close proxies for the well-documented earnings-change/earnings-momentum and net-debt-issuance anomalies.

The MIN is taken over two incommensurate quantities — a cash change scaled by market cap (typically a few percent) versus a change in the dlc/lt fraction (dispersion an order of magnitude larger) — so the "weakest-link" gate will be mechanically dominated by the smaller-scale cash term rather than genuinely requiring both improvements; normalize (rank or z-score) both legs before combining.

This is a well-motivated diagnosis of the archived signal's fmb/alpha disagreement, combines two commensurate industry z-scores so the signed minimum is a legitimate soft conjunction, and the expected negative sign matches the expression's direction; the main risk is that the profitability leg alone carries the result.

Replacing symmetric volatility with the profitability floor is a substantive, well-argued refinement, but unlike the archived version the numerator now changes sign across firms, so dividing by the always-positive asset-to-market term shrinks the signal toward zero for profitable cheap firms — implying cheapness is a negative for healthy firms and breaking the stated "valuation as compensation" interpretation over half the cross-section.

Units are consistent and the conjunctive turnaround story is distinct from the archived static sales-yield composites, but the current-liability-reduction leg mechanically raises working-capital accruals, so the positive expected sign runs against the accrual anomaly and the mechanism deserves an explicit accrual control.

This is largely a re-aggregation of the archive's "Dual-Cushion Recovery Value" (same three ingredients, MIN instead of multiplication plus industry z-scoring), and since ΔRE/AT is essentially net income minus dividends over assets, the retained-earnings leg reintroduces plain profitability rather than the claimed independent "repair" channel.

The reclassification-vs-repayment critique is legitimate and the construction is internally consistent, but one leg is literally identical to the archive's "Standardized Cash-Funded Maturity Repair" and the other is a near-mechanical respecification of its partner, so the result will be highly collinear with an already-tested signal.

The stated diagnosis (that falling current liabilities mechanically inflate working-capital accruals, i.e., the accrual anomaly) is not addressed by adding cash accumulation, since Δcash sits outside operating accruals, and the triple nested MIN will collapse to whichever standardized leg is weakest, leaving an unstable, thinly-populated long tail on top of an already-tested claim-light sales signal.

Economically coherent and internally consistent (both legs high implies genuinely funded payout value), and distinct from the archive's deleveraging-based dividend conditioner, though much of the long-short spread may come from a de facto dividend-payer dummy in the low tail, so a payer-only sample check is warranted.

The conjunction is sign-consistent and economically interpretable, but the second leg is effectively the negative of the well-known RE/ME value-quality proxy, so the incremental content rests entirely on the Δoancf interaction and the test should control for RE/ME standalone.

This is the mirror image of the archive's "Standardized Cash-Funded Maturity Repair" built from the negated versions of the same two components, so it is close to a sign-flipped rediscovery whose only genuine novelty is MIN-over-negatives selecting the max rather than the min of the original pair.

This is a single-operator tightening (TS_MIN over 3 years) of the archived Current-Claim After-Tax Operating Yield, with no mechanism addressing why that parent's alpha was economically small and imprecise (ls_talpha 1.19), so it reads as a cosmetic persistence variant rather than a substantive improvement.

It is only a one-leg substitution on the archived Standardized Cash-Funded Maturity Repair, but the swap from cash-stock accumulation to operating-cash-flow improvement is an economically meaningful quality-of-cash distinction (cash balances can rise from issuance or asset sales) and the expression, sign, and standardized soft-AND construction are internally consistent.

This merely re-scales the two legs of the archived Deficit-Confirmed Cash Collapse (deficit moved from market to assets, cash-flow change moved from assets to market), and the name is internally misleading since the cash-flow leg is market-scaled, making it a denominator permutation rather than a new mechanism.

The stated adjustment is inconsistent with the accounting: oancf already nets working-capital changes, so subtracting DELTA(lct) double-penalizes payables growth while also deducting short-term debt changes (dlc) that are financing rather than operating, so the expression does not cleanly compute the hypothesized "cash flow not attributable to current-liability financing."

The integrated residual (operating cash flow less dividends less any uncovered current-claim gap, market-scaled) is a coherent and non-trivial combination that plausibly fixes the dividend-payer selection problem in the archived residual-cash signal, though it inherits the dimensional awkwardness of subtracting a balance-sheet gap level from annual flows.

The two legs are close repackagings of the well-documented asset-growth and debt-issuance anomalies, and the first leg's expected sign runs directly against that literature (shrinking assets historically predict higher, not lower, returns), so the negative sign rests entirely on an unargued interaction effect.

Internally consistent and coverage-motivated, but it is a one-variable swap (che/lct for oancf/lct) inside the already-tested MIN(after-tax operating yield, liquidity leg) template from generation 7, i.e. a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism, and substituting a static cash stock for the cash-realization channel removes precisely the corroboration that drove the earlier alpha.

The multiplicative weighting is a genuinely different functional form from the archive's MIN-based deficit/cash-collapse conjunction, the non-negative RANK weight preserves the signed direction so the expression matches the stated hypothesis and negative sign, and coverage should improve; the main caveat is that IND_ZSCORE recenters at the industry mean, so the claimed "no signal when cash flow is unchanged" neutral point is only approximate.

The dimensional-coherence critique of the earlier funding-gap subtraction is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the construction simply re-pairs two already-tested archive legs (post-dividend cash-flow yield and the net-working-capital ratio from the generation-0 signal) inside the same MIN template while inheriting the dvc/oancf coverage constraint of ~0.08.

This is the most substantive departure in the batch — replacing raw asset contraction with valuation-scaled asset-turnover improvement is an economically distinct channel and the cash-cushion leg is well motivated — though the reviewer should note that change in asset turnover is itself a published DuPont-decomposition anomaly (Soliman), so the novelty rests entirely on the valuation scaling and the cash conjunction.

The expression does encode the stated trap, but it loads positively on dividend yield — a leg the archive shows carries a weakly positive return slope — while expecting a negative overall sign, so the two components pull against each other, and the second leg is the exact negation of the generation-6 residual-cash dividend signal, making net direction and incremental content ambiguous.

Both legs have already been tested in the archive and both failed in this direction — lct/lt produced a wrong-signed positive alpha in the generation-4 concentration trap and the market-scaled cash-flow decline was insignificant in generation 7 — so mechanically MIN-ing two known-weak components inside the same template offers little reason to expect improvement, and oancf still caps coverage near 0.08.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals — the numerator of "Post-Payout Liquidity Residual" (oancf−dvc) with the denominator of "Uncovered-Claim After-Tax Yield" (mktcap + current-liability gap) — and moving the gap from numerator to denominator is a cosmetic reformulation of essentially the same economic content, at the lower ~0.08 oancf coverage.

Substituting the margin leg of the DuPont decomposition for the turnover leg of the archived "Cash-Backed Asset Productivity Recovery" is a defensible substantive channel change rather than a pure clone, though the scaling term collapses to Δmargin × (sale/mktcap), so part of the leg is a repackaged sales-to-price value exposure that must be controlled for in interpretation.

The construction is internally consistent (both AND-ed legs are high-is-bad, matching the negative expected sign), the flooring at zero correctly avoids picking up an inverted dividend-yield exposure, and replacing the archived signal's static current-claim weight with a deterioration condition is a genuine diagnosis-driven change rather than a cosmetic tweak.

This is the archived "Deficit-Weighted Working-Capital Depletion" with che substituted for wcap in an otherwise identical expression — a one-variable cosmetic swap whose parent already produced a wrong-signed Fama-MacBeth slope (+2.795 against a negative expectation), and it overlaps further with the archived "Liquidity-Reserve Depletion Trap."

Replacing liability growth with an actual uncovered current-claim level is a coherent response to the parent signal's slope/alpha disagreement, but the MAX(lct−act,0) leg is zero for the majority of firms, so its industry z-score is near-constant for most of the cross-section and the MIN will produce heavy ties that may blunt the portfolio sort.

This is the archived MIN(...)/mktcap "repair" template with legs already tested separately in "Market-Scaled Dual-Cushion Repair" (Δche) and "Claim-Light Sales Recovery" (−Δlct), and the −Δlt component is close to the well-documented net debt issuance / net external financing anomaly.
